title: The soul of the fast
hookLine: the fast is a shield, so don't shout or quarrel (Bukhari)

lines: THE LAST HOUR, A LONG LINE.
cards: Five in the evening, the last hour of a long fasting day. Blood sugar is low, traffic is worse, and someone cuts in line at the store. Every part of the body wants to say something sharp.
The past days were about the rules: the intention, what breaks the fast, who's excused, how days are made up. All of it about the stomach.
But the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said something about the fast that has nothing to do with food, and everything to do with that moment in the line.

teach.h: JUNNAH: THE FAST IS A SHIELD.
teach.b: First, the image. In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet ﷺ says the fast is a junnah, a shield, held up between you and what would hurt you.
In the same report he says what it's for: when one of you is fasting, don't speak obscenely and don't shout. And if someone insults you or picks a fight, say: I am fasting. Not a comeback.
A reminder, as much to yourself as to them.

teach.h: NO LIES, OR THE FAST IS HOLLOW.
teach.b: Second, without this, the fast can go hollow. Another report in Bukhari is blunt: whoever doesn't give up lying and acting on lies, Allah has no need of them giving up their food and drink.
An empty stomach and a sharp tongue, in this report, don't add up to a fast.

Third, it connects to the purpose surah two gave on the first day of this part: the fast is prescribed so that, in Pickthall's words, "ye may ward off (evil)." The shield and the warding off are close pictures.
In this reading, hunger is the training, and what's guarded is what comes out of a person when they're tired and provoked.
Fourth, the same report carries a saying from Allah, a hadith qudsi: every deed of a person is for them, except fasting, which is for Allah, and Allah rewards it.

teach.h: A SECRET BETWEEN A PERSON AND ALLAH.
teach.b: Some teachers say that's because no one else can see a fast: a secret between a person and Allah, whose proof shows in how they treat the person in front of them.
Fasting or not, the shield works the same way: one sentence, said quietly, before the sharp one.

how: Muslims who are fasting try to guard their speech and temper as well as their stomachs, and when provoked some say, as the Prophet taught, "I am fasting."

games.q: what does “the soul of the fast” mean?
o: the fast as a shield that guards the tongue and temper
the meal before dawn that gives strength for the day
the hunger that makes the body weak by evening

games.q: the soul of the fast — tap the pairs.
p: Allah has no need of the hunger

s: as long as you don't eat or drink, the fast is complete, whatever you say
a report in Bukhari says Allah has no need of the hunger of someone who won't give up lies.
the Prophet ﷺ called the fast a shield
junnah, a shield, in Sahih al-Bukhari.
the report tells a fasting person to answer an insult with a sharper one
it says: say, I am fasting.

games.q: it's the last hour of your fast, and someone insults you to your face. what does the report in Bukhari say to do?
o: stay silent and walk away without a word.
answer back, but keep it polite.
games.why: say: I am fasting. the fast is a shield, and the shield is a sentence.

practice: Picture where your temper is most likely to slip today, a meeting, a commute, a sibling, a comment section, and see it coming.
Choose your shield sentence: if you're fasting, it can be the Prophet's, I am fasting; if not, any short line that reminds you who you mean to be.
Say it silently on each out-breath until it feels ready, and if you pray, ask Allah for patience.

wordCard.voice: The soul of the fast. The fast as a shield: no shouting, no quarreling, no lies; and when provoked, I am fasting. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a shield, a covering; the Prophet's word for the fast.

carryVoice: Your line: a shield. The fast guards the tongue, not only the stomach. Until tomorrow.
